metaTitle: Akwantukese Festival of New Juaben in Koforidua
metaDescription: Akwantukese is the New Juaben festival in Koforidua, remembering the great migration from Juaben in Ashanti. When it is held, what happens and how to go.
subtitle: New Juaben’s great journey
answer: Akwantukese, “the great journey”, is the festival of the New Juaben Traditional Area, centred on Koforidua in the Eastern Region. It remembers the migration of the Juaben people and their allies from their homes in Asante to found New Juaben in the 1870s, and it runs for about a month to a procession and grand durbar in Koforidua, usually in November or December.

sections.title: The great journey
sections.html:
The festival marks the great migration of the Juaben people and their allies from their ancestral homes in Asante to settle in the Eastern Region and found New Juaben, with Koforidua at its centre. The 2013 festival marked 135 years since that journey.[[2]]

Akwantukese was instituted by Daasebre Professor Oti Boateng, Omanhene of New Juaben, in the 1990s, to strengthen unity, encourage self-help development and teach the young the area’s origins.[[1,3]]

sections.title: What happens
sections.html: The festival runs for about a month and ends with a procession of chiefs and people through the main streets of Koforidua and a grand durbar. In 2013 the durbar was on 14 December at Jackson Park.[[2]] In 2019 it was on 23 November.[[1]]

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: Koforidua is the capital of the Eastern Region, about 90 minutes north of Accra.
Check the dates: the traditional council sets the days each year, often only weeks ahead. Local radio and the national press carry the announcement.
Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.

faq.a: The great journey, remembering the migration of the Juaben people from Asante to found New Juaben.
Usually in November or December, ending with a grand durbar in Koforidua.
